claims.claim: Iraq's state oil tanker company shipped two million barrels of crude on a VLCC to outside the Strait of Hormuz, the first such assignment in decades.
claims.episode_span: shipped two million barrels of crude on a very large crude carrier to a point outside the Strait of Hormuz
claims.source_title: Iraq transports its oil past Hormuz for first time in decades as war with Iran chokes exports
claims.supporting_quote: The state-run Iraqi Oil Tankers Company shipped two million barrels of crude on a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) to outside the strait, its director general Ali Qais told the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

claims.claim: Ali Qais said the shipment shifted part of Iraqi oil sales from free-on-board Basra to delivery outside the strait.
claims.episode_span: shifting part of Iraqi sales from free-on-board loading at Basra to delivery outside the strait
claims.source_title: Iraq transports its oil past Hormuz for first time in decades as war with Iran chokes exports
claims.supporting_quote: The task was assigned to the company for the first time in decades, shifting part of Iraqi oil sales from the previous free on board (FOB) Basra port model to deliver outside the strait, Mr Qais added.

claims.claim: Iraq depends on oil for at least 90 percent of state revenue, and most prewar exports of roughly 3.3 million barrels a day went through Hormuz from Basra.
claims.episode_span: oil provides at least 90 percent of state revenue, and that most exports — roughly 3.3 million barrels a day before the war
claims.source_title: Iraq transports its oil past Hormuz for first time in decades as war with Iran chokes exports
claims.supporting_quote: Iraq, Opec's second-largest producer, depends on oil for at least 90 per cent of state revenue. Most of its exports, roughly 3.3 million barrels per day before the war, went from its southern Basra terminals through the Strait of Hormuz.

claims.claim: The National reports the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed by Iran since the war broke out in February.
claims.episode_span: the waterway has been effectively closed by Iran since the war broke out in February
claims.source_title: Iraq transports its oil past Hormuz for first time in decades as war with Iran chokes exports
claims.supporting_quote: The narrow waterway has been effectively closed by Iran during the war, with shipping disrupted by missile and drone attacks, insurance spikes, and naval confrontations.

claims.supporting_quote: Iranian-aligned factions launched drones toward Gulf states from Iraqi territory, prompting Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan to hold Baghdad responsible.

claims.supporting_quote: Iraq has been able to export three million barrels of oil per day since the beginning of September, the state news agency quoted oil minister Bassim Khudair as saying last month.

claims.claim: Ethiopia's Catholic bishops on Thursday grieved armed conflict in Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia and other regions and called for dialogue.
claims.episode_span: the Church grieves over armed conflict in Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia and other regions
claims.source_title: Ethiopia's Catholic Bishops issue pastoral appeal for peace and reconciliation
claims.supporting_quote: The message began by stressing that the Ethiopian Catholic Church grieves deeply over the armed conflict currently present in Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia, and other regions of the country.

claims.claim: Pope Leo said at his Wednesday General Audience that hostilities had broken out again in Tigray, Afar and Amhara and asked all parties to choose dialogue.
claims.episode_span: Pope Leo, who at his Wednesday General Audience said he was following renewed hostilities in Tigray and neighbouring Afar and Amhara
claims.source_title: Ethiopia's Catholic Bishops issue pastoral appeal for peace and reconciliation
claims.supporting_quote: The African Bishops echoed Pope Leo's appeal for peace at his Wednesday General Audience, after his return from his Apostolic Journey to France, where he said he was following with deep concern the situation in Tigray and in the neighboring regions of Afar and Amhara, where hostilities have once again broken out.
